messages:
Noah (Finance): AP put CloudLine inv 2026-CL-519 on hold. Vendor is asking for a $1,200 backcharge for out-of-scope GPU-hours but our usage logs don't match. Can AP confirm hold reason? :clipboard:

Tara (Accounts Payable): AP bot flagged PO mismatch + disputed quantity. We have PO 4220 for CloudLine with pre-approved 8,000 GPU-hours. Invoice 2026-CL-519 shows 9,600 hrs @ $0.075 = $720. Vendor is requesting a separate backcharge invoice for $1,200 referencing "overage reconciliation". Need docs: signed approval for overage or evidence of mutual agreement.

Irene (Vendor Ops): CloudLine emailed saying on-demo usage exceeded estimates due to burst testing; they included csv usage export and a note from their Sales AE saying "please bill overtime at v1 rate" but no signed amendment. I asked for the AE to confirm in writing to finance.

Noah (Finance): For audit we need either (A) PO increase with approval chain, (B) signed amendment referencing effective date and updated quantities/rates, or (C) documented email thread with explicit approvals from Redwood procurement + Finance that we can keep for retrospective PO adjustments. Phone calls won't cut it.

billing-bot: Invoice 2026-CL-519 uploaded by Irene; status = HOLD_REASON = PO_MISMATCH + QUANTITY_DISPUTE.

Tara (Accounts Payable): If vendor wants to charge $1,200 extra we need a signed change order. Otherwise AP treats the extra as disputed and will not pay. If vendor provides usage CSV we will reconcile but still need approval to shift PO amounts.

CloudLine Billing: Our AE confirmed in thread: "We authorize billing of confirmed overage at $0.125/hr for burst period Jan 28-30, see attached usage CSV." (attachment: usage_jan28-30.csv). Requesting expedited payment.

Marta (Legal): We can't accept unilateral AE authorization as a contract amendment. Any additional charges require a signed amendment or a formally approved credit/charge memo with Redwood sign-off. Also check whether the burst was covered under contractual "trial bursts" clause.

Irene (Vendor Ops): CloudLine says contract has a trial-burst clause but Sales applied it inconsistently. Vendor offered two remedies: 1) reissue invoice excluding disputed hours (they'll invoice accepted hours only) OR 2) provide signed amendment and updated PO references. They asked if we can do a fast-track approval since they processed payroll.

Noah (Finance): Fast-track only with Procurement + VP Finance approval and a written amendment. I don't want to set precedent for AE-level billing changes.

Tara (Accounts Payable): I'll keep hold. If vendor reissues excluding disputed hours and references PO 4220 we'll pay the undisputed portion. For any overage we require Procurement approval and a signed amendment before AP will pay. Ticket #AP-7839.

CloudLine Billing: Understood. Reissuing a corrected invoice for the undisputed amount and opening a separate change request for the overage. Will upload shortly.

billing-bot: New invoice 2026-CL-519v2 uploaded; matched to PO 4220 for 8,000 hrs. Dispute note linked to AP ticket AP-7839.

Noah (Finance): Thanks. Please confirm vendor will not pursue collections while dispute is open. Also add a vendor note: require signed amendment for any out-of-scope billing moving forward.

Irene (Vendor Ops): Confirmed with CloudLine: they will pause collections and submit amendment for overage approval. Closing loop once amendment arrives. :white_check_mark:

Marta (Legal): I'll review any amendment language for non-retroactivity and clear definition of "burst" triggers.
